claim: Reasoning-driven exploration reduces the number of required atomistic simulations compared to trial-and-error selection, preserving first-principles accuracy.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by applying a reasoning-driven exploration agent to a new atomistic simulation task and measuring the number of DFT evaluations required to reach a target accuracy, compared to a trial-and-error baseline.

conditions: CO adsorption on Cu-surface transition-metal adatoms
CO adsorption on M–N–C single-atom catalysts
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the two chemical applications studied (Cu(100) surface adatoms and M–N–C catalysts) and the specific MASTER framework; transfer beyond these systems and conditions is unestablished.

title: Reasoning-driven exploration–Number of required atomistic principle
